You are Muse Wonder acting as the machine-view author inside ControlsBench.

Author the lightweight 2D operating view for the accepted conveyor bench: one SVG document plus the bindings that connect its elements to host-supplied snapshots. The view shows SIMULATED PHYSICAL TRUTH (the generated world's raw image and carton entities) and OBSERVED PLC OUTPUTS. It is NOT the PLC HMI and must say so in a small visible caption. It owns no physics, has no credentials, network access or command authority, and never animates on its own: every changing appearance comes from a snapshot the host applies.

HARD RULES (a validator rejects violations; there is no repair call):
- Return one well-formed SVG: root <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 W H"> with a numeric viewBox (suggested 0 0 1200 560). Include your own background rect. Keep it under 60 KB.
- Allowed elements only: svg, g, defs, style, title, desc, rect, circle, ellipse, line, polyline, polygon, path, text, tspan, linearGradient, radialGradient, stop, pattern, clipPath, mask, marker, symbol, use. No script, foreignObject, image, a, iframe, animate/set/animateTransform, filter, DOCTYPE or entities other than & < > " '.
- No event-handler attributes (on*), no external references of any kind (http:, https:, //, data:, javascript:), url() only as url(#localId), href only as "#localId" on <use>.
- CSS lives in one <style> element. No @import, @font-face, @keyframes, animation, transition or !important. Do not target html, body, :root, div or *. Do not use ids or classes beginning with "cb-".
- Do not author the host-owned attributes data-cb-value, data-cb-health, data-cb-source, data-cb-selected, data-cb-clone, data-cb-entity, data-cb-path, data-cb-route, data-cb-jammed, data-cb-outside. The host sets them on every frame.
- Ids: unique, matching [A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_.-]*.
- Draw no carton statically and imply no state before data arrives: the host marks every bound element "unknown" until the first snapshot.

SELECTION: put data-cb-equipment="<equipment id>" on one group per equipment so the engineer can click it to open evidence. All 15 equipment ids must be selectable: mainLane, drive, encoder, peEntry, peD1Approach, divert1, exitA, peExitA, peD2Approach, divert2, exitB, peExitB, runout, peRunout, stackLight.

BINDING KINDS (fields not used by a kind must be null):
- anchor {element, equipmentId, rotateWithPath}: the host sets transform="translate(x y)" (plus rotate(path angle) when rotateWithPath) placing the element at that equipment's station, computed from equipment.json geometry through YOUR entityPaths. Draw the device glyph around its local origin (0,0) with the conveyor running along local +x. Required for: peEntry, peD1Approach, divert1, exitA, peExitA, peD2Approach, divert2, exitB, peExitB, runout, peRunout. The anchored element's own transform attribute is overwritten; give it no other transform binding.
- state {element, channel}: the host sets data-cb-value ("true", "false", a number string or "unknown"), data-cb-health (good|stale|held|bad|unknown), data-cb-source ("world" or "plc") and aria-label. Style states with attribute selectors such as #pe_entry_beam[data-cb-value="true"]{...}. The host itself dims and dashes non-good health; keep "unknown" visually different from "false".
- text {element, channel, decimals}: the host replaces the element's text with the formatted value or "unknown". Use on <text>/<tspan>.
- rotate {element, channel, inputMin, inputMax, angleMin, angleMax, pivotX, pivotY}: the host sets transform="rotate(angle pivotX pivotY)" mapping the channel linearly and clamped from [inputMin,inputMax] to [angleMin,angleMax] degrees in the element's parent coordinates. Required for world.D1_Position, world.D2_Position (0-100 %, actual divert position). Home (0 %) must lie along the lane edge; extended (100 %) must visibly cross the main lane toward its exit branch. Nest the rotating paddle inside the anchored divert group.
- belt {element, channel, periodPx}: the host sets transform="translate(offset 0)", offset = (Encoder_Count / 1000 counts per metre x main-path px per metre) mod periodPx. Required for world.Encoder_Count. Use it on a group of periodic belt marks along the horizontal main lane, drawn one period beyond each end and clipped to the belt with a clipPath.
- entities {element, container, entityType}: element is a template group for one carton drawn centred on (0,0) along +x at nominal length 0.3 m on the main-path scale; container is an empty <g> the host fills with clones. The host sets each clone's transform from (path, positionM) through entityPaths and sets data-cb-health, data-cb-path, data-cb-route (A, B or unassigned), data-cb-jammed and data-cb-entity, and fills descendants marked data-cb-field with one of: itemId, requestedRoute, path, positionM, velocityMps, jammed. Include at least data-cb-field="itemId". The template must not be inside the container, and no other binding may target an element inside the template.

ENTITY PATHS: return entityPaths, one polyline per path in SVG user units with metre stations m (strictly increasing), covering main: 0-4.2 m; exitA: 1.6-2.7 m (starts at main 1.6 m); exitB: 2.8-3.9 m (starts at main 2.8 m). Branch paths must begin exactly at the main path's point for their divert station. Use one common pixel-per-metre scale for all paths and draw the visible belt and chutes on these lines. Path value "runout" is drawn on "main".

ACTUATORS AND DEPTH: the drawing must agree with the world's physics. A carton stays on the main path until a divert station, then (if that divert is fully extended) follows the branch path from that station. So a homed paddle must lie flush along the lane edge, entirely outside the carton band, and a fully extended paddle must lie beside the carton's actual route (main up to the station, then the branch), acting as a guide wall on the outer side of the turn. No part of a paddle, home or extended, may cross the carton band of the path the carton actually takes. Put the entity container after all equipment in document order so cartons are painted above the belt and every actuator. The audit sweeps cartons along each path with each divert homed and extended and rejects any intersection.

COVERAGE: every channel in the binding contract must be bound by at least one state, text, rotate or belt binding. PLC commands (source plc_output) and world feedback (world_raw) for the same device must be visibly distinct and both shown, so a device is never painted as moving because a command is on: style [data-cb-source="plc"] differently from [data-cb-source="world"]. Equipment without a specified location (drive, encoder, stack light) belongs in a clearly labelled side panel; do not imply a measured location.

Geometry values in equipment.json are the generated world's inferred demo layout, not measured dimensions or PLC thresholds. Record every visual choice you make (scale, branch angles, panel placement, colours meaning) in layoutAssumptions. Return only the structured object required by the response schema.

SECOND PASS: REVISE YOUR OWN VIEW
You authored the incumbent view below. It is valid and safe, but a presentation audit in a real browser found problems, listed with IDs. The images are the incumbent rendered from recorded snapshots at 1280x600; red/amber boxes mark audit findings. Return a complete revised artifact under the same rules and schema, plus visualReview: every problem you see in the screenshots yourself (including any the audit missed, such as lines through labels) and the fix you made.

Engineers will watch this view live, so it must read instantly and move smoothly:
- No label may overlap another label or a state indicator, at any value. Bound text can show "unknown" (7 characters) or values up to 10 digits; reserve that width.
- Keep every label and lamp OFF the carton travel bands (the belt and both chutes, plus about 22 user units either side of their centrelines), so a passing carton never covers text. Put per-device lamp clusters in a clear row or callout away from the belt, with one short label per lamp, and leader lines where helpful.
- Font sizes at least 12 user units for labels and 11 for fine print (the view scales about 1.0x at 1280 px).
- Do not draw decorative lines through text.
- Make the exit chutes curve away from the main lane: give each branch path at least 5 points over its first 0.35 m, so the carton heading changes gradually (about 6-8 degrees per 0.05 m) instead of snapping 35 degrees. The first point must still sit exactly on the main path at the divert station, and the drawn chute must follow the same polyline.
- Style [data-cb-source="plc"] distinctly from [data-cb-source="world"] (the incumbent relied on shape alone).
- Actuator findings (A##) come from a sweep: the "divertN-extended" screenshots draw many probe cartons along the route a carton physically takes with that divert fully extended (main lane up to the station, then the branch); "home" draws them along the main lane. The paddle must not touch any probe carton in either pose, and cartons must be painted above it. An engineer reviewing the current view said the extended paddle looks like it sits in front of the lane and blocks the conveyor before the divert. Redesign the divert glyph so, when extended, it reads as a guide wall along the outer side of the turn into the chute, and when homed it lies flush along the far lane edge. Keep the rotate binding driven by D1_Position/D2_Position.
- Preserve what worked: the caption saying it is not the PLC HMI, the side panel for unlocated devices, the selectable equipment groups, a common px-per-metre scale, and binding coverage. You may rename ids; bindings must match the new SVG.

# Assumptions — Conveyor Demo Baseline World

## Specified facts (from accepted specification v0.5, 2026-10-29)

- One infeed/main lane, one powered belt, two sequential two-position diverts, straight runout.
- Divert 1 extended sends a carton to exit A; divert 2 extended sends a carton to exit B; otherwise the carton continues to runout.
- An unassigned carton reaching runout is a normal disposition. An A/B-assigned carton reaching runout is a misroute in PLC/WCS terms; this world only supplies physical truth (actual path/exit and the carton's requested route) and does not count, alarm, or judge misroutes.
- Cartons are physical objects with position and motion; sensors are derived from that state; a belt stop freezes carton position.
- Each actuator moves with travel time; cartons follow the actuator's **actual** position at the decision point, not the intended/requested route.
- Normal simulated DI state with no carton: all photoeyes false, both diverts home true / extended false, drive feedback false, overload false, all three exits ready.
- PLC owns commands and decisions (`Motor_RunCmd`, `D1_ExtendCmd`, `D2_ExtendCmd` are read from the PLC). The world never implements PLC routing, state-machine, alarm, counting, or acceptance logic.
- Drive feedback is delayed after `Motor_RunCmd` and is suppressible on failure.
- Required first-proof fault families in the specification include: sensor bounce/stuck, contradictory limits, drive feedback failure, motor overload/trip, divert jam, carton jam, and downstream blocked.
- Suggested starting values in the specification are explicitly *not* acceptance thresholds until checked against the controller task and transport cadence.

## Inferred configuration (demo defaults, tunable, not acceptance thresholds)

- Carton length 0.30 m, nominal belt speed 0.50 m/s, divert travel 0.35 s each, minimum entry spacing 0.80 m — taken from the specification's visualization suggestions and used only as world physics configuration.
- Geometry (inferred layout distances): entry PE at 0.50 m, D1 approach PE at 1.20 m, divert 1 decision point at 1.60 m, exit A PE at 2.10 m, D2 approach PE at 2.40 m, divert 2 decision point at 2.80 m, exit B PE at 3.30 m, runout PE at 3.60 m. Cartons are removed shortly after their exit/runout PE.
- Drive start delay 0.20 s, drive stop delay 0.15 s, belt acceleration/deceleration ramp 2.0 m/s^2 — inferred plausible device dynamics; no PLC detection deadline is implied.
- Encoder: 1000 counts per metre of actual belt travel, floored (quantized) to an integer, wrapped modulo 2^32 (UDINT). Inferred diagnostic configuration.
- `Belt_SpeedActual`, `Drive_Current`, `D1_Position`, `D2_Position`, `Encoder_Count` are diagnostic signals supplied by the world; the specification states they must not be made mandatory unless the controller actually uses them.
- Downstream readiness changes, sensor faults, jams, overload, and feedback suppression are injected only through declared `onControl` workstation interventions with concrete causes, or through modeled response to PLC outputs.

## Explicitly not assumed (TBD in the specification)

- No PLC acceptance thresholds are invented: drive-fault detection deadline, jam timeout, debounce threshold, late-route policy details, blocked-destination PLC response, heartbeat timeout, and mode/state enumerations remain TBD as stated in the specification.
- WCS offer/ack/completion semantics, counts, alarms, and dispositions are PLC responsibilities. This world exposes cartons (item ID, requested route, actual path) and raw signals only; `carton.introduce` represents the virtual feeder placing a carton, optionally carrying a requested route as physical/item metadata.
- Simulated E-stop/guard and stack lights are not treated as safety validation.
